name: intraday_volatility_breakout_5s
author: adapted from claude_strategist
thesis: When a stock's intraday ATR on 1-min bars suddenly expands (ATR_10 > 2 * ATR_60), it signals the start of a regime change from low-vol to high-vol. The direction of the first volatility expansion bar tends to persist for 10-30 more bars because the trigger (news, block deal, institutional flow) takes time to fully disseminate. Edge persists because detecting real-time volatility expansion requires continuous monitoring of ATR ratios across stocks, which most traders don't do.
mechanism: Volatility compression (squeeze) indicates that market makers have tightened their quotes around a narrow range. When a catalyst breaks the equilibrium, the compressed energy releases as participants rush to reposition. The thin order book beyond the compression zone allows rapid price movement with minimal resistance.

filters.vix_filter: vix < 28 (some vol is good, but extreme chaos is not)

weaknesses: Volatility expansion without directional persistence = whipsaw; common during news-driven spikes
Higher slippage (4 bps) during high-vol bars reduces effective edge
ATR_10 on 1-min can spike due to a single large bar and then normalize immediately — false signal
prior_art: Volatility breakout (Keltner Channel concept) — adapted for ATR-ratio-based detection on 1-min
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; apply to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index instead of FnO universe; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
